verdict.rationale: Grok Bot runs on a persistent cloud computer with a filesystem, and named Bots keep their files across sessions. A files-and-results page lists file types such as CSV, JSON, YAML, source code and Jupyter notebooks, and a community user reports a Bot generating a design and sending it as a .ai file. That shows the product can create files, but documents, presentations, iterative editing and export are never explicitly documented. Missing for 10: explicit document/presentation creation, a documented iterative-editing workflow for files, a documented export/download path, independent corroboration for office-style documents.

support.subject: As a knowledge-worker, I can have the assistant create and iteratively edit documents, presentations, and other files I can export

citations.quote: Your Bots run on a persistent cloud computer with a browser, filesystem, and terminal
A named Bot keeps its memory, files, browser sessions, and preferences across sessions
CSV, JSON, YAML, and source-code files ... Jupyter notebooks
It worked with a 'prototyper' bot that generated a pattern from the user's logo and sent it to the supplier as a .ai file.
